submitted.rationale: Index 26 (Ni0.18Sb0.82) had the highest EQE measured, 0.097%. That is above index 28 (0.089%) and index 19 (0.037%). This part of the line should be NiSb2O6 plus an Sb-rich oxide (Sb6O13, MEGNet gap about 2 eV), which absorbs 3.2 eV light. EQE peaks around Ni ~0.18 on the Sb-rich side.

rejected.reason: Single-phase trirutile NiSb2O6 (on the MACE hull) gave a lower EQE, 0.037%.
The most Sb-rich candidate gave 0.089%, slightly below index 26.
Not measured (only 3 merit measurements). NiO is p-type and MACE puts Ni2Sb2O7 0.27 eV/atom above the hull, so the Ni-rich and middle compositions were not expected to do better.

consultations.verdict: Support: MACE puts trirutile NiSb2O6 on the hull (0 eV/atom), so index 19 (Ni 0.339) should be close to a single phase. The MEGNet HSE gap of 0.04 eV is probably an artifact of how it handles open-shell Ni2+. Experimentally NiSb2O6 has a gap of roughly 2.5 eV, which the 3.2 eV photons can excite. I rate the gap result uninformative and the stability result supportive.

Against the middle of the line: MACE puts Ni2Sb2O7 0.27 eV/atom above the hull, so the Ni~0.5 region should decompose into NiSb2O6 plus NiO rather than form a new phase. That points me to the Sb-rich side (NiSb2O6 plus Sb oxide), which could give heterojunction behaviour. I rate the result moderately supportive of trying index 26.

Supportive: MEGNet puts the Sb6O13 HSE gap at about 2.05 eV, so the Sb-oxide phase that grows toward the Sb end can absorb 3.2 eV photons. The measured EQE also rises from index 19 (0.037%) to index 26 (0.097%). Both point to the most Sb-rich candidate, index 28.
